criteria.opaque_with_constructors: Declare one opaque type per closed set in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and add a constructor operation per member (4 make_kind constructors, 7 observe_kind constructors, 3 hostile_descriptor constructors, 5 read_op constructors: 19 new ops) that take no arguments and return the opaque type. Can call sites name members only through constructors, so an unlisted string can never flow into a closed parameter. The 7 sets without authoritative tables stay plain str. Each constructor needs its own checker admission clause and emitter mapping, and every TS table edit must add or retire a constructor in the same change.
criteria.str_with_checker_allowlist: Declare every closed-set parameter as str in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json. The new NT-I01 checker admission module mirrors the four authoritative tables (NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS with 4 members, NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS with 7 members, NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS with 3 members, NATIVE_READ_OPS with 5 members) and rejects any call whose closed-set argument is not a string literal exactly equal to a table member, following the checkBrowserTag precedent in compiler/internal/check/browser.go. The 7 sets with no table (fault_mode, registered_runtime, registered_api, registered_operation, reviewed_fault_target, observer_id, scope_ref) stay plain str with review-enforced membership documented. The observe_kind note claiming 9 members is treated as drift; the 7-member const is mirrored and the note filed as a K-lane finding.
criteria.variant_unit_leaves: Declare the 4 table-backed sets as Can variants in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json with one unit leaf type per member (4 make_kind leaves, 7 observe_kind leaves, 3 hostile_descriptor leaves, 5 read_op leaves: 19 new leaf types), so the type checker itself rejects unlisted members without any literal inspection. The 7 sets without authoritative tables stay plain str. Every TS table edit must add or retire a leaf type in the same change, and each leaf needs emitter support to lower it to its wire string.

closed_set_modeling.instructions: Which closed-set modeling best preserves the native-values closedness contract in the Can catalogue with the least unreviewable surface?

state: We are merging the native-values capability (I01) into the Can toolchain: the service contracts in tools/runtime/test-services/native-values/schema.ts, session.ts and observe.ts must become callable Can operations through compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json plus a new NT-I01 checker admission module. The services validate pre-dispatch string sets in two tiers. Tier 1 is runtime-validated by const tables with includes() checks: NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS (primitive_bits, text, ordered_entries, hostile_descriptor) in session.ts, NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS (scalar_tag, ieee_bits, lexeme, descriptor, entries, identity, counters) in observe.ts, NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS (getter_then, throwing_thenable, revoked_proxy) in session.ts, and NATIVE_READ_OPS (bits, text, entries, property_then, call_then) in observe.ts. Tier 2 has no table and no validator anywhere: fault_mode (the schema.ts catalogue note claims absent, throw, revoked, counted_delegate but no const exists), registered_runtime, registered_api, registered_operation and reviewed_fault_target (no member lists at all), and observer_id and scope_ref (ID-pattern strings only). One drift is confirmed: the observe_kind catalogue note in schema.ts claims 9 members (adding bytes and events) while NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS holds 7; the const is authoritative. Hard constraints: catalogue.json has no enum kind and rejects unknown fields (DisallowUnknownFields), so the proposal nativeTest block is dropped; variants need one type leaf per member; opaque types without constructors cannot be built from Can; the checker can read static string literals (checkBrowserTag precedent in compiler/internal/check/browser.go) while the I04 http_peer precedent used open str; closedness must be enforced by mechanism, never by naming convention.
